- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70% from prior 18d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >75% above 18d mean, reduce by 5–10% to align with historical volatility.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and event supply is high, model underestimates volatility; increase forecast variance by 1–3% to reflect uncertainty.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to lag; add 1–3 days of delay in price adjustment to reflect event impact.
